long_biography.plain_text:
When Sudan nationalised several Izmirlian family businesses in 1970, Dikran Sarkis Izmirlian established a new operating base in Geneva. The decision redirected an enterprise rooted in Sudanese cotton farming, oilseed exports, machinery distribution and contracting. From Switzerland, he built international commodity-trading operations around peanuts, with processing plants in the United States, Africa and Latin America.

Cotton-ginning and oilseed-processing machinery became another major field, and the group became a global leader. Izmirlian also developed substantial commercial and agricultural property holdings in Europe and the United States. More London, a large office complex beside Tower Bridge, and the neighbouring Hilton reflected the scale of that expansion. His work joined trading, industrial equipment and property within one family-controlled investment group.
